page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.c8ae.large is an x86_64 compute-optimized instance hosted on the KVM hypervisor. It is powered by a dedicated AMD EPYC 9T34 processor clocked at 3.4 GHz, configured with 1 physical core presenting 2 vCPUs via simultaneous multithreading. Hardware cache includes 32 KB of L1d, 1.0 MB of L2, and 32 MB of shared L3 cache. Memory is provisioned at 4.0 GB (2.0 GB per vCPU), and the network tier provides a 3 Gbps baseline bandwidth. The configuration includes no integrated local storage and no hardware GPU accelerators, requiring reliance on external block storage volumes for persistent data.

Benchmark data reflects strong single-threaded processing capabilities alongside the expected throughput constraints of a 2-vCPU envelope. In single-core evaluations, the server achieves top-tier results in stress-ng (3111.68) and a strong Geekbench single-core score of 1997.0, aided by modern instruction extensions such as AVX-512 (including VNNI and BF16) and cryptographic acceleration via AES and SHA-NI. Large-block uncached memory operations register in the middle tier, yielding 47.32 GB/sec read and 27.49 GB/sec write bandwidth.

Because aggregate compute capacity is bound to a single physical core, multi-core and aggregate system benchmarks fall into lower percentile brackets. Multi-threaded stress-ng scores (3113.59), Geekbench multi-core (2481.0), and PassMark database operations (1075.1) show clear limits in parallel capacity. Similarly, throughput-dependent services such as static web serving (2.87 GB/sec) and Redis SET operations (2.88 million operations/sec) demonstrate baseline rather than scale-out performance.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the ecs.c8ae.large offers dedicated CPU allocation with high per-thread instruction throughput without the overhead of excess memory or unused storage arrays. It is best suited for compute-bound, low-concurrency utility workloads, including lightweight CI/CD pipeline tasks, single-threaded processing jobs, microservices, and modest web serving endpoints.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.c8ae.large is a compute-optimized instance built on the x86_64 architecture and KVM hypervisor, featuring an AMD EPYC 9T34 processor running at 3.4 GHz. It delivers 2 dedicated vCPUs mapped across 1 physical core, accompanied by 4.0 GB of system memory, 32 MB of L3 cache, and a 3 Gbps baseline network interface. The instance includes neither local SSD storage nor dedicated GPUs, requiring external storage attachments. Benchmarks emphasize exceptional single-core compute performance, placing in top percentiles for single-threaded stress-ng and Geekbench tests, supported by AVX-512 and hardware cryptographic instructions. However, its small core count limits multi-threaded throughput across database and concurrent workloads. The instance serves cost-conscious environments requiring high per-core performance for lightweight microservices, single-threaded batch tasks, and low-traffic web serving.
